description: Concept types above feeds: what kind of thing a field is, whichever feed or SIEM it comes from. A feed concept names its type and inherits the type's meaning fragment, default role, value shape and hazards.

principal.label: Principal
principal.description: The identity that acted: an ARN, a UPN, a SID. The key for 'everything this actor did'.

user_id.label: User id
user_id.description: A stable, opaque identifier for a user or account: an object id, an IAM principal id, a SID. Survives renames; not human-readable.

user_name.label: User name
user_name.description: A human-readable account or display name. Not unique across domains or tenants and changes on rename.

account_id.label: Account or tenant id
account_id.description: The account, subscription or tenant a record belongs to. A qualifier for every other key in the record.

access_key.label: Access key id
access_key.description: The id of a credential that signed a request. Follows the credential, not the person holding it.

session_id.label: Session id
session_id.description: Ties together the records of one session or authentication flow.

app_id.label: Application id
app_id.description: The client or resource application involved, as an id. Names change; ids do not.

source_ip.label: Source address
source_ip.description: The network address a request or sign-in came from, as the receiving service saw it.

dest_ip.label: Destination address
dest_ip.description: The network address a request or flow was addressed to, as the sending or reporting service saw it.

hostname.label: Hostname
hostname.description: A host's name as it reported it or as DNS gave it. Repeats across domains and changes on reimage.

host_id.label: Host id
host_id.description: A sensor's or platform's stable identifier for a host. The host key when names are not.

domain.label: Domain name
domain.description: A DNS name: an endpoint, a host header, a service.

user_agent.label: User agent
user_agent.description: The client's self-description. Set by the client and trivially spoofed; good for noticing change, not for attribution.

process_id.label: Process id
process_id.description: An operating-system process id. Recycled by the OS: meaningful only with the host and a time bound.

process_uid.label: Sensor process id
process_uid.description: A sensor's own unique id for a process, never recycled within a sensor session. Pivot on this, scoped by host id.

command_line.label: Command line
command_line.description: The full command a process started with.

file_path.label: File path
file_path.description: A path on disk or an object key.

file_name.label: File name
file_name.description: A file's base name without its directory.

file_hash.label: File hash
file_hash.description: A cryptographic digest of a file's contents. The key for 'everywhere this binary ran', across hosts and feeds.

signing_id.label: Signing identifier
signing_id.description: The identifier a binary's code signature carries: on macOS a reverse-DNS string such as com.apple.contactsd. A label the signer wrote into the signature, not proof of who signed it.

team_id.label: Team id
team_id.description: The Apple developer team whose certificate signed a binary, a ten-character id. Empty (or a placeholder such as '-') for Apple's own platform binaries, which are signed by Apple's chain rather than a team.

bitmask.label: Bit flags
bitmask.description: Several yes/no facts packed into one integer, one per bit. Read by mask, never by equality: two values that differ in one bit share every other flag.

event_time.label: Event time
event_time.description: When the thing happened at the source, as opposed to when the SIEM received it.

record_type.label: Record type
record_type.description: Which kind of record this is within the feed; decides which other fields are present.

event_id.label: Event id
event_id.description: A unique id for one record. Deduplicate on it.

request_id.label: Request id
request_id.description: The id of one request or flow, shared by every record it produced.

outcome.label: Outcome
outcome.description: How the operation ended: a result code, an error code, success or failure.

event_source.label: Event source
event_source.description: The service or component that produced or received the operation.

region.label: Region
region.description: The cloud region or geography a record is about.

resource_id.label: Resource id
resource_id.description: The identity of a resource an operation touched: an ARN, an object id, a bucket, an instance.

raw_object.label: Nested object
raw_object.description: A structured value whose shape depends on the record type. Reached by path (dotted in Splunk, dynamic in KQL).

flag.label: Flag
flag.description: A yes/no fact about the record.

enum.label: Enumeration
enum.description: One of a fixed set of values; a decode table gives their meaning.

identifier.label: Identifier
identifier.description: An opaque id whose kind the feed defines.

nat_vpn.text: One address is many people behind NAT, a proxy or a VPN egress. 'From this address' groups a network, not a person.

hostname_unstable.text: A hostname is what the host was told; it repeats across domains and changes on reimage. Use the platform's host id as the key.

client_supplied.text: Set by the client and trivially spoofed. Use it to notice change, not to attribute.

pid_recycling.text: Operating-system process ids are recycled. Pivot on the sensor's own process id where there is one, and always scope by host; a bare PID across hosts means nothing.

per_host.text: Unique per host, not across hosts: always pair with the host id.

names_not_stable.text: Names change on rename and repeat across domains and tenants; the stable id behind the name is the key.

time_basis.text: Event time and ingest time differ by delivery lag. A tight upper time bound can miss the newest records.

signer_chosen.text: A signing identifier is chosen by whoever signed the binary: anyone can sign a build as com.apple.anything. Only the certificate chain makes it Apple's (Apple's platform signing carries no team id); check the hash, the team id and the path against a known-good corpus before trusting the name.

team_id_is_the_certificate.text: A team id names the developer account whose certificate signed the binary, not who built or ran it. Certificates leak and get revoked; a known team id says who paid for the certificate.
